Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

judge verb

form an opinion of; decide

also judging by, judge for yourself, pass judgement, pass judgment, assess

classical

Ter. Ad. 564: abī, virum tē jūdicō
Cic. Amic. 85: cum jūdicāris, dīligere oportet

jūdicō, jūdicāre, jūdicāvī, jūdicātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

judge: weigh up and decide; hold, consider

To try a case and to judge in the everyday sense alike. With a double accusative, judge someone to be: virum tē jūdicō, I judge you a man. From which one can judge: ex quō … jūdicārī potest (Cic. Amic. 23).

Other words

  • dījūdicō, dījūdicāre, dījūdicāvī, dījūdicātum — judge between, decide which is right

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 5.2.23 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: to judge by discerning or distinguishing; to decide, determine.

Examples

  • Laudō, Ctēsiphō; patrissās: abī, virum tē jūdicō.

    Well done, Ctesipho, you take after your father. Off you go: I judge you a man.Ter. Ad. 564

  • cum jūdicāris, dīligere oportet, nōn, cum dīlēxeris, jūdicāre

    you should judge first and then love, not love first and then judgeCic. Amic. 85

  • Ex quō quantum bonī sit in amīcitiā jūdicārī potest.

    From this one can judge how much good there is in friendship.Cic. Amic. 23

See also think, judge.
